name: What drywall finish level do I need for my basement walls and ceiling?

mainEntity.name: What drywall finish level do I need for my basement walls and ceiling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Level 4 is the standard finish for most residential basement living spaces, while Level 5 is recommended for areas with critical lighting. A Level 4 finish includes taped joints, three coats of joint compound over fasteners and seams, and thorough sanding, which provides a smooth surface for flat or eggshell paints and light textures. A Level 5 finish adds a full skim coat over the entire board surface to eliminate subtle texture differences between the drywall paper and compound. Level 5 is ideal for ceilings under recessed downlights or walls receiving semi-gloss paint.
acceptedAnswer.description: Level 4 is standard for most basement walls, while a Level 5 skim coat is best under harsh, direct lighting or when using higher-sheen paints.
